_about: Hand-curated qualitative context gathered by the analyst on 2026-09-28 from public news and official sources. Used only to EXPLAIN results, never as an input to scores. Re-verify before relying on it.

notes: SFO's two pairs of parallel runways are only ~750 ft apart, far below the ~4,300 ft normally needed for independent parallel approaches, so arrival capacity depends on special procedures and weather.
In spring 2026 the FAA stopped side-by-side visual approaches to the closely spaced runways (with concurrent runway repaving), cutting the arrival rate from ~54 to ~36 per hour even in clear weather.
From 12 Aug 2026 staggered parallel approaches raised the cap to ~40 arrivals/hour, with ~42 planned by end of August - still well below the old ~54.
Marine-layer fog / low ceilings regularly trigger FAA Ground Delay Programs that push the rate back down to ~36.
John Wayne Airport operates under the 1985 Settlement Agreement (amended 2014, in force through 2030) that caps annual passengers: 11.8M from 2021, potentially rising to 12.5M from 2026.
A noise curfew bans commercial departures 10pm-7am (8am Sundays) and arrivals 11pm-7am, in place through 2035.
Congestion at SNA is therefore largely regulatory (a legal cap) rather than physical; terminal expansion cannot add passengers beyond the cap.
Anchorage is primarily a cargo gateway: ranked #1 US airport for air cargo and #3 worldwide in 2025 rankings, serving transpacific freighters that refuel/transload between Asia and North America.
Most long-haul departures are all-cargo flights to Asia; passenger service is mostly within Alaska and to the lower 48.
'LA' is ambiguous: the Los Angeles region is served by LAX plus Burbank (BUR), Long Beach (LGB), Ontario (ONT) and Santa Ana / John Wayne (SNA).
